findings.quote: Hosing removes some of the smoke if it is done within a day of a fire.
findings.note: PARTIALLY answerable blind: published smoke-taint work shows hosing/washing fruit does not remove volatile phenols already taken into the berry, so A and C ('Their fruit held less of the smoke compounds') are eliminable on domain knowledge alone, leaving B and D. Blind pick B (~50% between B and D). The mechanism is domain reasoning, not a form-visible tell, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: They take up the phenols and keep them there.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: leaf-uptake studies of smoke taint report that vine leaves absorb volatile phenols with little translocation to the bunches, so a domain reader leans D over its mirror-image A with no passage. Blind pick D. A/B/D are parallel substantive mechanisms and C names a real viticultural practice, so no structural tell exists; flag, not kill.

findings.quote: Some of the ashy finish is made in the taster’s own mouth, not the glass.
findings.note: PARTIALLY/WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: B overclaims ('a trained taster will always find it') and D is a sweeping dismissal ('Panels of this kind cannot be trusted'), both eliminable on form; the remaining A-vs-C choice is then decided by well-documented in-mouth, saliva-mediated release of bound smoke phenols, which points to C. Blind pick C. Form alone only narrows to two, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Whatever the tray has caught stays on it, because the wind presses in at those joints.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: cavity-tray and weep-hole behaviour under driving rain (wind pressure at the openings holds water back on the tray until the pressure drops) is standard building-fabric knowledge and selects D. The stem's own framing 'before the wind drops' additionally makes D the only wind-referencing option, a mild lexical-overlap tell. A/B/C remain substantive accounts a passage could ground, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick D.

findings.quote: Because the table charged by the night, a heavy bill marked an owner slow to miss his beast.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: C is the only option that supplies its own warrant, and it is the coherent inference given general knowledge that village pounds charged poundage per night. D presumes the pound-keeper controlled how long a beast stayed, and B makes the bill turn on the day of the week — both weak on general reasoning about how pounds worked. Narrows to C by domain reasoning rather than pure form, so flag. Blind pick C.

findings.quote: Kalkkorn i stenen svällde när de tog upp fukt efter bränningen.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: this is textbook lime blowing (free CaO in fired brick hydrating and expanding after the burn), so a domain reader picks C with no passage. Corroborated inside the same sheet by q:3, whose option B names 'kalkspräckt tegel' and whose stem presupposes watering of the finished bricks. B and D name substantive alternative mechanisms (in-kiln bursting, too-rapid cooling), so flag rather than kill. Blind pick C.

findings.quote: En del av förlusten flyttades från kundens mur till bruksgården.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: B overclaims ('kom inga klagomål'), A asserts a mechanism that is false on domain knowledge (watering does not harden brick or improve frost resistance), and C contradicts the point of the practice. D is the only hedged, genuinely inferential option and follows logically from the lime-blowing mechanism already named in q:1, so two-plus options fall blind. Blind pick D.

findings.quote: Luften förvärmdes av svalnande stenar och rökgaserna torkade nästa gods.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: heat recuperation — incoming combustion air preheated by the cooling ware while waste flue gas dries the next green batch — is the standard textbook explanation of Hoffmann ring-kiln fuel economy, so A is pickable blind. B is additionally self-defeating ('brann hetare än den gamla ugnen, och veden räckte därför längre') and D answers a different question (skärmtaken, not fuel per thousand). C is substantive, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick A.

findings.quote: Att besparingen blir en bråkdel av den budgeterade.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: the critical-column genre prior plus the absolute-versus-hedged contrast between D ('inte sparar en enda krona') and C narrows the field, and q:2's option A ('Nästan alla berörda elever åker med turer som ändå körs') corroborates a near-zero-but-not-zero saving. Materially better than chance blind, but A and B are not cleanly eliminable on form alone, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick C.

findings.quote: De flesta av hållplatserna ligger vid vägsträckor som kommunen har bedömt som olämpliga att gå längs.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: the stem names the method (pupil addresses laid over the timetables), which cannot yield D's road-safety judgement, and B's 'Kostnaden per tur sjunker' is a cost claim rather than a mapping finding — both eliminable on form with no domain knowledge. A and C remain near-paraphrases of one another that only the passage separates, so flag rather than kill. Blind pick A.

findings.quote: Formen bars vidare av en stomme som sparades, medan lövningen kunde läggas om ändå.
findings.note: PARTIALLY plus cross-question corroboration: A ('Varje by har medvetet bevarat') and B (scope creep from pole form to the whole midsommarfirande) are eliminable as overclaims on form alone, and q:1's stem presupposes a real saved-frame versus unsaved-frame contrast that defeats C's 'mätningar räcker inte'. D also echoes the sibling stem's 'sparade stommen' vocabulary, leaving it essentially decided blind. Blind pick D.
